review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its simp lemmas relate to the rest of the CartierDivisor development. The simp lemmas isoSheafOfRestrictEq_hom_sheafι, toLineBundleClass_principalCartierDivisor and toLineBundleClass_zero look sound. toLineBundleClass_zero is reachable from the simp lemma principalCartierDivisor_one, so the two do not compete. toLineBundleClass_add and toLineBundleClass_neg (in Picard.lean) are also simp and agree with them. I found no cycle or competing rules. The one weakness is the missing unfolding lemma for `toLineBundleClass`. I had no way to run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemma compiles. The finding is a modest ergonomics issue, not a bug.

findings.excerpt:
def toLineBundleClass : LineBundleClass X :=
  LineBundleClass.mk D.toInvertibleSheaf
findings.problem: `toLineBundleClass` is a plain def. It has no unfolding equation (`toLineBundleClass D = LineBundleClass.mk D.toInvertibleSheaf`). The only way to reach the underlying class is `toLineBundleClass_eq_mk_iff`, which forces an `Iso` goal. Four downstream files each re-prove the same equation as a local `have hmk`. They go through `toLineBundleClass_eq_mk_iff.mpr` and `simpa only [toInvertibleSheaf_obj]` or `rw [toInvertibleSheaf_obj]`, then supply `Iso.refl _` or `eqToIso`. The simp set cannot reach `LineBundleClass.mk` lemmas such as `mk_eq_one_iff`, `mk_tensorProduct` or `eulerDegree_mk`, because `toLineBundleClass` is opaque to it. The workaround is the same boilerplate each time.
findings.proposed_change: Add a `rfl` unfolding lemma next to the def: `lemma toLineBundleClass_eq_mk_toInvertibleSheaf (D : CartierDivisor X) : D.toLineBundleClass = LineBundleClass.mk D.toInvertibleSheaf := rfl`. Do NOT tag it `@[simp]`: that would unfold the class and stop `toLineBundleClass_add`, `toLineBundleClass_neg`, `toLineBundleClass_zero` and `toLineBundleClass_principalCartierDivisor` from firing. Use it with `rw` or `simp only`. Replace the four local `hmk` proofs with it. The def could also take `@[irreducible]` or be left as is, with this lemma as the single entry point.
findings.benefit: Callers can unfold the class in one step and move to the `LineBundleClass.mk` simp lemmas. The repeated `have hmk … := by apply toLineBundleClass_eq_mk_iff.mpr; simpa only [toInvertibleSheaf_obj] …` blocks go away. The `@[simp]` lemmas on `toLineBundleClass` keep their precedence, so there is no new expansion and no cycle.
